$description: GENERATED by tools/build-surface-recipes.cjs from core/tokens/surfaces.json and core/assets/prismata.css. Never edit it by hand: change the stylesheet or the vocabulary and rebuild. tests/core-contracts.cjs fails when this file is out of date. Each surface in surfaces.json has one record. Its recipe is what the stylesheet resolves for an element wearing only the surface selector, written as the stylesheet writes it: token references such as `var(--pr-resin-fill)`, literals such as `999px`, and expressions such as `calc(var(--pr-radius) + 6px)`. A platform resolves the tokens from its own export (core/exports/prismata-tokens.ts, .swift, .kt), so every platform reaches the same values. Fields: `fill` is the element's own background (the winner of `background` and `background-color`). `blur` and `saturation` are the arguments of `blur()` and `saturate()` in its `backdrop-filter`. `rim` is the border the browser draws: the `border` shorthand, with its colour replaced by a `border-color` that cascades after it (noted under `diagnostics`), or `border-color` alone when there is no shorthand. `shadow` is `box-shadow`, `radius` is `border-radius`, `padding` is the `padding` shorthand. `haze` is the feathered paint layer: a pseudo-element that draws a fill through a blur filter, which is how Prismata paints Haze and Stone so the foreground stays crisp. When `haze` is present the element's own `fill` is usually `transparent`, and the visible reading fill is `haze.fill`. `feather` is the blur of the feathered paint, on the element or on that layer. `extras` holds every other declaration on the element. `layers` holds every pseudo-element the recipe paints, keyed by its name. `fallbacks` holds the four adaptations: `opaque` under `[data-effects=opaque]`, `reducedTransparency` under `@media (prefers-reduced-transparency:reduce)`, `forcedColors` under `@media (forced-colors:active)`, and `noBackdropFilter` under `@supports not (backdrop-filter...)`. Each lists only the declarations that change and win, as `declarations` for the element and `layers` for pseudo-elements. A null branch changes nothing. `conditions` holds other conditional branches the same way, keyed by the condition. `shadowed` lists declarations a branch makes that lose to the base recipe in the cascade and therefore never render. `missing` names what the surface's materials oblige the recipe to carry and the stylesheet does not supply for this selector, and `why` says why it cannot (the selector is a part of the surface, or takes the value from what it is worn on). Rules that add a state or a variant the surface selector does not name (`:hover`, `.primary`, `span.pr-field-shell`, descendants such as `.pr-dock button`) are not part of a recipe, because the element described does not wear them. `tokens` lists every `--pr-*` custom property the record references. A selector that expands to elements the stylesheet paints differently, such as the checkbox and the radio, carries `alternatives`: one recipe per element, keyed by the element selector, in place of the top-level fields.

surfaces.name: Haze reading surface
diagnostics: rim composed from the border shorthand (1px solid var(--pr-edge)) and border-color (transparent), which cascades after it
rim composed from the border shorthand (1px solid var(--pr-edge)) and border-color (transparent), which cascades after it

surfaces.name: Resin control

.pr-control.why: Takes the radius of what it is: the pill comes with `.pr-button`, and a card-shaped control keeps the content radius of the surface it also wears.

button.why: Takes the radius of what it is: the pill comes with `.pr-button`, and a card-shaped button keeps the content radius of the surface it also wears.

surfaces.why: Element-keyed: `.pr-button` coats a `button` or an `a`. On any other element, wear `.pr-control`, which coats any element.

.pr-editor.why: A part: the document inside the field shell, which carries the Resin surround and the Haze well.

.pr-field-shell.block.why: The shell's display only: worn with `.pr-field-shell`, which carries the coat.

.pr-tag.why: The tag's geometry (the pill, the 48px floor, the type size), worn with `.pr-resin-haze`, which carries the coat.

surfaces.name: Stone label backing

.pr-media-caption.why: A part: the outer element positions the cue, and its inner box (`.pr-media-caption > *`) carries the Stone backing and the radius.

.pr-media-caption.large.why: The reader's caption style, larger: `--pr-caption-scale` multiplies the cue's 15px to 28px range on its inner box. Worn with the cue's own recipe.

.pr-media-caption.larger.why: The reader's caption style, largest: `--pr-caption-scale` multiplies the cue's 15px to 28px range on its inner box. Worn with the cue's own recipe.

.pr-media-caption.solid.why: The reader's caption style, solid: the inner box's backing is the opaque surface with no feather, the backing the cue's fallbacks draw. Worn with the cue's own recipe.

surfaces.why: Stone backs a label and takes the radius of the element it backs.

surfaces.name: Dialog
diagnostics: rim composed from the border shorthand (1px solid var(--pr-outline)) and border-color (var(--pr-rim)), which cascades after it

.pr-dialog-body.why: A part: the scrolling body inside the dialog's Haze surface, which carries the material; the body adds the scroll contract.

surfaces.name: Authored bubble
diagnostics: rim composed from the border shorthand (1px solid var(--pr-edge)) and border-color (transparent), which cascades after it

.pr-table.why: A part: the table inside `.pr-table-scroll`, which carries the Resin shell and the Haze fill; the table is transparent on it.

.pr-dock-inner.why: The Stone label backing inside the dock. The dock carries the Resin blur, and Resin never contains Resin, so the inner fill has none.

surfaces.name: Selection control
surfaces.note: Prismata paints this surface on native elements by element selector rather than a class. The recipe is what the stylesheet gives that element.

input[type=range].why: A track and a thumb, painted on the slider's pseudo-elements (`::-webkit-slider-runnable-track`, `::-webkit-slider-thumb` and their `::-moz-range-` forms), which this record does not read.

.pr-choice.why: The box alone: the mark inside it and the colour of a selected box are drawn by the component that wears it.

.pr-choice.radio.why: The box alone, round: the dot inside it is the component's.

diagnostics: rim composed from the border shorthand (1px solid var(--pr-rim)) and border-color (var(--pr-outline)), which cascades after it
.pr-choice.outline.why: The box alone: the mark inside it and the colour of a selected box are drawn by the component that wears it.

surfaces.name: Native control furniture
surfaces.note: Prismata paints this surface on native elements by element selector rather than a class. The recipe is what the stylesheet gives that element.

surfaces.name: No surface of its own
surfaces.note: This surface has no material of its own. A component made of it inherits whatever it sits on, so there is no recipe to publish.
